properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 13 at 9:37AM PDT until October 16 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY NEW FIRE STARTS
THURSDAY THROUGH FRIDAY DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY STRONG SANTA
ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.Moderate to locally strong Santa Ana winds will quickly develop
on Thursday, peak Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon,
then weaken through the weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will settle
over the region and dry out any helpful effects of the recent
rains. Fire weather watches are now in effect, which will likely be
upgraded to Red Flag Warnings by Wednesday. Some areas may see Red
Flag conditions linger into Saturday. Interior Santa Barbara and
San Luis Obispo Counties may also see Red Flag conditions on
Friday, and a Fire Weather Watch is being considered.

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a
Fire Weather Watch for wind and low relative humidity, which is
in effect from Thursday morning through Friday evening.

* WINDS...Northeast winds 20 to 40 mph with gusts of 50 to 70 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable for
extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and property.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are likely to occur in the coming days. Residents near wildland
interfaces should prepare now on what to do if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information..

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 13 at 8:39AM PDT until October 13 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and elevated surf are expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be expected
near times of high tide.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT this
afternoon. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 5 PM PDT
this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There
is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.1
feet this morning. The Beach Hazards Statement will likely be
extended into Thursday morning due to minor tidal overflow from
continued elevated tides and surf.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Calhoun, SC; Richland, SC
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 13 at 11:08AM EDT until October 16 at 12:48AM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in South
Carolina...

Congaree River At Congaree River at Congaree NP Near Gadsden
affecting Richland and Calhoun Counties.

Congaree River At Carolina Eastman affecting Richland, Lexington
and Calhoun Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Congaree River at Congaree River at Congaree NP Near
Gadsden.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Flooding begins in the Congaree National
Park. This will begin to produce flooding of portions of the lower
boardwalk. At 17.0 feet, The access road to the Sandy Run
subdivision becomes flooded. The lower boardwalk in the Congaree
National Park becomes flooded by Cedar Creek. At 18.0 feet, Several
homes in the Sandy Run subdivision along the river become flooded.
At 18 feet the river covers the Weston Lake overlook in the
Congaree National Park. Between 18 and 18.5 feet the river begins
to cover sections of the elevated boardwalk.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 16.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:00 AM EDT Tuesday was 16.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.4 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Most flooding deaths occur in vehicles. Never drive through a flooded
roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL LATE THURSDAY NIGHT
